# Fill

Header: `winui/ui/panels/Fill.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panels/Fill.hpp`.

A child of a stack that is given the room the other children leave. Built by [ui::Fill](#uifill).

A [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol) measures its children unbounded along its axis. A fill is measured last, with the room left over as its bound, so a scrolling child inside it (a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll), a [ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview)) gets a real height and scrolls. Several fills, and the stack's spacers, share the room by their weight. Where the stack itself has no bound along its axis (inside a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll)) there is nothing to share, and a fill is as big as its content. Outside a stack it is a plain one-child container.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  page = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
page->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Inbox"));
auto* fill = page->add(std::make_unique<ui::FillControl>());
fill->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>());
page->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("3 unread"));
```

## `ui::Fill`

Gives one child of a stack the room the other children leave. Builds a [ui::FillControl](#uifillcontrol).

In a [VerticalStack](stack.md#uiverticalstack) of a header, a list and a footer, putting the list in a [Fill](#uifill) keeps the footer at the bottom and lets the list scroll in between.

A stack gives each child what it asks for along its axis, with no limit, so a list in a plain stack grows as long as its items and never scrolls. A [Fill](#uifill) is measured with the room the other children leave. Several fills share that room by [`.weight`](#uifill-weight), together with the stack's spacers. A [ui::Spacer](spacer.md#uispacer) is a [Fill](#uifill) with nothing in it. In a stack that has no limit itself (one inside a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll)) a [Fill](#uifill) is measured as big as its content, and takes what room the stack is arranged with beyond that.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::vector<std::string>> messages;
ui::Property<int>                      unread{0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing = 8,
    .content = {
        ui::Text{.text = "Inbox", .role = ui::TextRole::Subtitle},
        ui::Fill{.content = ui::ListView<std::string>{.items = messages}},
        ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(unread, [](int n) { return std::format("{} unread", n); })},
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Fill{
    .weight, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uifill-weight"></span>`weight` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{1.0f}` | This fill's share of the leftover room, relative to the other fills and spacers in the same stack. |
| <span id="uifill-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uifill-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uifill-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uifill-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uifill-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uifill-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uifill-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Fill>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uifill-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | What gets the room. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::FillControl](#uifillcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::FillControl`

Derives from `ui::ContentHost`.

A child of a stack that is given the room the other children leave. Built by [ui::Fill](#uifill).

A [StackControl](stack.md#uistackcontrol) measures its children unbounded along its axis. A fill is measured last, with the room left over as its bound, so a scrolling child inside it (a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll), a [ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview)) gets a real height and scrolls. Several fills, and the stack's spacers, share the room by their weight. Where the stack itself has no bound along its axis (inside a [Scroll](scroll.md#uiscroll)) there is nothing to share, and a fill is as big as its content. Outside a stack it is a plain one-child container.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  page = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
page->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Inbox"));
auto* fill = page->add(std::make_unique<ui::FillControl>());
fill->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>());
page->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("3 unread"));
```

### FillControl

```cpp
FillControl() = default
```

An empty fill of weight 1.

### weight

```cpp
float weight() const
```

This fill's share of the leftover room, relative to the other fills and spacers in the same stack.

### set_weight

```cpp
void set_weight(float weight)
```

Sets the share; negative is treated as 0. Updates the layout.
